requirements.title: File view and tree hash
requirements.rationale: The cache, the language counts and the map must agree on what the repository is, and the same content must hash the same inside and outside the box.

criteria.condition: the file view is built for a `--dir` inside a git work tree
criteria.action: list tracked files plus untracked files that are not ignored, read with `git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard` through a new NUL-separated `gitx` list method, and drop files that no longer exist in the working tree
criteria.contract: a file named with a space and a non-ASCII character appears unquoted; an ignored file and a deleted tracked file are absent

setup: a temporary git repo built like gitx newRepo (skipped when git is missing)

a tracked file `a b.txt`, an untracked file `é/ü.go`, a file matched by .gitignore, a tracked file deleted from the working tree, a `.agent-fox/x` file and a tracked path under `.git`-like name `sub/.gitkeep`
check.pseudocode: v = FileView(ctx, dir); assert 'a b.txt' in v; assert 'é/ü.go' in v; assert 'ignored.log' not in v; assert 'deleted.txt' not in v; assert v == sorted(v); assert none(p.startswith('.agent-fox/') or p.startswith('.git/') for p in v)

criteria.condition: the file view is built for a `--dir` that is not inside a git work tree
criteria.action: walk `--dir` with the standard library, skipping directories named `.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `node_modules`, `vendor`, `target`, `dist`, `build`, `__pycache__`, `.venv` and `venv`
criteria.contract: no path in the view has one of those names as a directory segment

setup: a plain temporary directory (no .git) holding src/a.go and, inside it, directories .git, .hg, .svn, node_modules, vendor, target, dist, build, __pycache__, .venv, venv and .agent-fox each with a file
a nested `src/vendor/x.go`
check.pseudocode: v = FileView(ctx, dir); assert v == ['src/a.go']; for p in v: assert not (set(p.split('/')[:-1]) & SKIP)

criteria.action: exclude `.git/` and `.agent-fox/` from both forms of the file view and return paths slash-separated, relative to `--dir`, sorted in byte order
criteria.contract: paths are in ascending byte order with no duplicates; no path begins with `/`, contains a backslash, or starts with `.git/` or `.agent-fox/`

setup: a generator of directory trees with random names including spaces and non-ASCII, both inside and outside a git work tree
check.pseudocode: for tree in gen_trees(): v = FileView(tree); assert v == sorted(set(v)); assert all(not p.startswith(('/', '.git/', '.agent-fox/')) and '\\' not in p for p in v)

criteria.action: compute the tree hash as SHA-256 over the file view's entries in order, where a regular file contributes its kind, executable bit, path and content SHA-256, a symlink its target without following it, and any other file type its type
criteria.contract: a 64-character lowercase hex string

setup: a temporary directory with a regular file, a symlink to a missing target, and (where the OS allows) a named pipe
check.pseudocode: h1 = TreeHash(dir); assert re.match('^[0-9a-f]{64}$', h1); chmod +x f; assert TreeHash(dir) != h1; relink(l, 'other'); assert TreeHash(dir) != h2

criteria.action: for any two directories whose file views hold the same paths, contents, executable bits and symlink targets, produce the same tree hash regardless of the commit HEAD points at, the absolute location of the directory or the content of ignored files, and for any one-byte change to a file in the view produce a different tree hash
criteria.contract: the two hashes are equal; the hash after changing one byte of a viewed file differs from before; the hash after changing only ignored files equals the one before

setup: a generator of small file sets with random content, exec bits and symlinks
two git repos with different commit histories and absolute locations
check.pseudocode: for fs in gen_filesets(): a=mk(fs, history=1); b=mk(fs, history=3); write_ignored(b); assert TreeHash(a)==TreeHash(b); flip_byte(a, pick(fs)); assert TreeHash(a)!=TreeHash(b)

criteria.condition: a file in the view cannot be read
criteria.action: hash a fixed `unreadable` marker in that entry's place and continue
criteria.contract: the tree hash is returned with a nil error

setup: a directory with a readable file and a file with mode 000 (test skipped when running as root)
check.pseudocode: h, err = TreeHash(dir); assert err == nil; assert h == TreeHash(dir)[0]; chmod 644; assert TreeHash(dir)[0] != h

criteria.condition: a tree hash is about to be computed
criteria.action: create `<dir>/.agent-fox/` and its `.gitignore` when either is missing, reusing the spec-05 `.gitignore` content
criteria.contract: after the call `<dir>/.agent-fox/.gitignore` exists and `git status --porcelain` lists nothing under `.agent-fox/`

setup: a git repo with no .agent-fox directory
check.pseudocode: TreeHash(dir); assert exists('.agent-fox/.gitignore'); mkdir('.agent-fox/gate/x'); assert '.agent-fox' not in git('status','--porcelain')

criteria.action: provide a NUL-separated changed-path method that returns the paths differing from a ref (`git diff -z --name-only <ref>`) plus untracked, non-ignored files (`git ls-files -z --others --exclude-standard`), de-duplicated and sorted
criteria.contract: paths with spaces, leading or trailing spaces, or non-ASCII characters are returned byte-exact

setup: a git repo with a base commit
after it: a modified tracked file ` lead.txt` with a leading space, a new committed file `é x.go`, an untracked `trail .txt ` and an ignored file
check.pseudocode: p = g.ChangedPaths(ctx, base); assert p == sorted([' lead.txt','é x.go','trail .txt '])

requirements.title: af lang detect and the gate table
requirements.rationale: The guard, the gate and the brain need one deterministic answer to what the repository is written in and how it is checked.

criteria.condition: `af lang detect [--dir D]` runs
criteria.action: report `languages`, each with its file count from the file view classified by extension over the outline's languages (Go, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, Java, Kotlin, Ruby, C, C++, C#, PHP, Scala, Lua, Bash), ordered by count descending then name, each carrying its root marker manifest when one exists, together with `gate`, `suite` and `programs`
criteria.contract: status `done`, exit 0; on an empty directory `languages` is empty and `gate.checks` is empty

setup: a repo with 3 .go files, 2 .py files, 2 .rs files and 1 .md file, plus go.mod
an empty directory
check.pseudocode: r = Detect(dir); assert [l.name for l in r.languages]==['go','python','rust']; assert r.languages[0].manifest=='go.mod'; assert Detect(empty).gate.checks==[]

criteria.condition: `<dir>/.agent-fox/gate.json` exists and parses as `{"version": 1, "checks": [...]}`
criteria.action: use its checks as the effective gate table
criteria.contract: `gate.source` is `file`

setup: a repo with a Makefile `check` target and `.agent-fox/gate.json` = {"version":1,"checks":[one custom check `./ci.sh`]}
check.pseudocode: r = Detect(dir); assert r.gate.source=='file'; assert [c.argv for c in r.gate.checks]==[['./ci.sh']]

criteria.condition: no `gate.json` exists
criteria.action: detect the table from root-level files only: a `GNUmakefile`, `makefile` or `Makefile` with a `check` target gives `[make check]` (kind `check`); otherwise a Makefile with a `test` target gives `make lint` (kind `lint`, only when that target exists) then `make test` (kind `test`); otherwise each language manifest adds its checks in the order Go, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, Java, and other languages add none
criteria.contract: `gate.source` is `detected`; every check has `name`, shell-free `argv`, `kind`, `source` (e.g. `Makefile:check`) and `available`; on this repository languages[0] is `go` and the checks are exactly `[make check]`

setup: fixtures: a Makefile with `check:`; a GNUmakefile with `test:` and `lint:`; a makefile with only `test:`; a go.mod with a Makefile that has `VAR := x` and `.PHONY` lines only; this repository's root
check.pseudocode: assert Detect(repoRoot).gate.checks == [Check('make check', ['make','check'], 'check', 'Makefile:check')]

criteria.action: derive language checks as: Go (`go.mod`) `go vet ./...` (lint) and `go test ./...` (test); Python (`pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `setup.cfg`, `pytest.ini`, `tox.ini`) `pytest` when a pytest signal exists (`pytest.ini`, a root `conftest.py`, `[tool.pytest`, or `pytest` named in pyproject, setup.cfg or requirements files) else `python -m unittest discover`, prefixed `uv run` with `uv.lock` or `poetry run` with `poetry.lock`, plus `ruff check .` (lint) when ruff is configured; Node (`package.json`) `<pm> test` when `scripts.test` exists and is not npm's placeholder and `<pm> run lint` when `scripts.lint` exists, with `<pm>` `pnpm`, `yarn` or `bun` by lockfile else `npm`; Rust (`Cargo.toml`) `cargo test`; Java `./mvnw test` or `mvn -q test` for `pom.xml` and `./gradlew test` or `gradle test` for `build.gradle(.kts)`, the wrapper form chosen when the wrapper file exists
criteria.contract: fixtures for a Go module, a pnpm Node package, a uv Python project, a Cargo crate and a Maven project each yield exactly the listed checks

setup: fixtures: go.mod; Cargo.toml; pom.xml without and with mvnw; build.gradle without and with gradlew; package.json with pnpm-lock.yaml and scripts test+lint; yarn.lock and bun.lockb variants; package.json with npm's placeholder test script `echo \"Error: no test specified\" && exit 1`; package.json with no lockfile

fixtures: pyproject.toml with uv.lock and `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` and `[tool.ruff]`; pyproject.toml with poetry.lock and pytest in requirements; setup.py only; tox.ini with a root conftest.py; pytest.ini only
check.pseudocode:
assert argvs(Detect(pnpmFixture)) == [['pnpm','test'],['pnpm','run','lint']]; assert argvs(Detect(placeholder)) == []
assert argvs(Detect(uvFx)) == [['uv','run','pytest'],['uv','run','ruff','check','.']]; assert argvs(Detect(setupOnly)) == [['python','-m','unittest','discover']]

criteria.action: report `suite` as the gate checks' argv plus `make check` and `make test` when those targets exist plus each detected language's full-suite form, and `programs` as the checks' argv[0] plus each detected language's toolchain programs, both de-duplicated in first-seen order
criteria.contract: on this repository `suite` contains `make check`, `make test`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...`, and `programs` contains `make` and `go`

setup: this repository's root
a fixture with a Makefile `check` target plus go.mod and Cargo.toml
check.pseudocode: r = Detect(repo); assert ['make','check'] in r.suite and ['go','test','./...'] in r.suite; assert 'make' in r.programs and 'go' in r.programs; assert len(set(map(tuple,r.suite)))==len(r.suite)

criteria.condition: `<dir>/.agent-fox/gate.json` exists but does not parse or names a version other than 1
criteria.action: fail without falling back to detection
criteria.contract: status `failed`, exit 1, error.category `config`, error.message names the gate.json path

setup: the af binary's lang detect command on a repo with a Makefile
case A: .agent-fox/gate.json holds `{not json`; case B: {"version":2,"checks":[]}
check.pseudocode: env, code = af('lang','detect','--dir',d); assert code==1 and env.status=='failed' and env.error.category=='config' and 'gate.json' in env.error.message

criteria.condition: a selected check's argv[0] does not resolve on PATH
criteria.action: keep the check in the table with `available: false` and emit the coded warning `check_unavailable` naming it, so that for any PATH the selected checks, their order and their argv are identical
criteria.contract: status `done`; warning code `check_unavailable`

setup: a fixture with go.mod and package.json (pnpm) and Cargo.toml
a generator of PATH values (empty, real, random subsets of the toolchain programs)
a repo with a Cargo.toml and PATH lacking `cargo`
check.pseudocode:
base = strip_available(Detect(fx, PATH=real)); for p in gen_paths(): assert strip_available(Detect(fx, PATH=p)) == base
env = af('lang','detect'); assert env.status=='done'; assert any(w.code=='check_unavailable' for w in env.warnings)

criteria.condition: `--write` is given
criteria.action: write the freshly detected table, ignoring any existing gate.json, to `<dir>/.agent-fox/gate.json` as `{"version": 1, "checks": [...]}` via a temporary file and rename
criteria.contract: a subsequent `af lang detect` reports `gate.source` `file` with the same checks

setup: a repo with a Makefile `check` target and an existing gate.json naming a different check
check.pseudocode: af('lang','detect','--write'); j=load('.agent-fox/gate.json'); assert j.version==1 and j.checks[0].argv==['make','check']; assert af('lang','detect').result.gate.source=='file'

requirements.title: af gate run
requirements.rationale: A red gate is a measured fact the loop decides from, so the gate must run each check credential-free and record exactly what happened.

criteria.condition: `af gate run [--dir D]` runs without a cache hit
criteria.action: run the effective table's available checks in table order in `--dir` under `gitx.ReducedEnvRunner`, writing each check's full combined output to `.agent-fox/gate/<id>/NN-<slug>.log` with NN the two-digit 1-based check index
criteria.contract: one log file per executed check; unavailable checks appear in `skipped` with reason `unavailable`

setup: a git repo with gate.json holding checks: `pass` (exit 0, prints 100 lines), `fail` (exit 3), `missing` (program that does not exist but is listed available:false... plus a check whose argv[0] exists in PATH only via a script that is removed before start to give error), and `slow` (sleeps past its per-check deadline in an internal test with a short deadline)
check.pseudocode: r = Run(ctx, dir, opts); assert r.checks[0].status=='pass'; assert len(r.checks[0].tail.splitlines())<=40 and len(r.checks[0].tail)<=4096; assert read(dir+'/'+r.checks[0].log).count('\n')==100

criteria.condition: `--hermetic` is given
criteria.action: run the checks under `gitx.HermeticRunner` with a freshly created temporary HOME and remove that HOME after the run, whether the run completed, failed or was cancelled
criteria.contract: result `hermetic: true`; the temporary HOME directory does not exist after the command returns

setup: a check script that writes `$HOME` to a file under the repo's .agent-fox/gate log
a second check that blocks until cancelled
check.pseudocode: r = Run(hermetic=true); h = read_log(r).home; assert r.hermetic and h != os.Getenv('HOME') and not exists(h)

criteria.action: record for each executed check `status` (`pass` on exit 0, `fail` on non-zero exit, `error` when the program could not start, `timeout` when the check's context expired), `exit_code`, `duration_ms`, `log` relative to `--dir`, and `tail` holding the last 40 lines of output capped at 4096 bytes
criteria.contract: each entry of `checks` carries status, exit_code (-1 for `error`), duration_ms, log and tail; a missing program yields status `error`, a check exceeding its deadline yields `timeout`

criteria.action: return a result holding `id`, `tree`, `table_source`, `hermetic`, `label`, `cached`, `passed`, `checks` and `skipped` (each with a reason), where `passed` is true only when at least one check ran and every executed check has status `pass`
criteria.contract: every result has id, tree, table_source, hermetic, label, cached, passed, checks and skipped with a reason per entry; passed is true for all-pass and for pass+skipped, false for one fail, false for no executed check

setup: tables: all pass; one fail; one pass plus one unavailable skipped; no available check
check.pseudocode: assert Run(allPass).passed; assert not Run(oneFail).passed; assert not Run(noneAvailable).passed

criteria.condition: one or more checks end with status `fail`, `error` or `timeout`
criteria.action: report the red gate as a measured fact
criteria.contract: status `done`, exit 0, `passed: false`

setup: case A: gate.json with one check `exit 1`; case B: gate.json whose only check program is not on PATH
check.pseudocode: env,code = af('gate','run'); assert code==0 and env.status=='done' and env.result.passed==false; assert 'no_checks' in codes(env.warnings) for case B

criteria.condition: the effective table has no available check
criteria.action: run nothing and return a result with an empty `checks` list
criteria.contract: status `done`, exit 0, `passed: false`, coded warning `no_checks`

criteria.condition: the tree hash taken after the checks differs from the one taken before them
criteria.action: keep and store the result under the earlier hash's id
criteria.contract: status `done`; coded warning `tree_changed_during_gate`; `tree` equals the pre-run hash

setup: a git repo whose single check appends a line to a tracked file
check.pseudocode: pre = TreeHash(dir); env = af('gate','run'); assert env.result.tree == pre; assert TreeHash(dir) != pre; assert exists('.agent-fox/gate/'+env.result.id+'/result.json')

criteria.condition: the command's own `--timeout` expires or a signal cancels the run
criteria.action: stop the running check's whole process group, store no `result.json`, and return the cancellation error to the shell
criteria.contract: status `failed`, exit 1; `.agent-fox/gate/<id>/result.json` does not exist afterwards

setup: gate.json with a check that spawns a child `sleep 60` and waits
`--timeout 1s`, and a second case that sends SIGINT
check.pseudocode: env,code = af('gate','run','--timeout','1s'); assert code==1 and env.status=='failed'; assert not exists(resultJson); assert not pid_alive(child)

requirements.title: Gate cache and labels
requirements.rationale: A gate the brain ran inside the box must be a cache hit for the landing gate, and the loop must address results by role.

criteria.action: compute the cache key as SHA-256 over the tree hash, the canonical JSON of the gate table and the runner mode (`reduced` or `hermetic`), and use the key's first 12 hex characters as the result `id` and the directory `.agent-fox/gate/<id>/`
criteria.contract: id is 12 lowercase hex characters and equals the first 12 characters of the independently computed SHA-256; reduced and hermetic ids differ; a different table gives a different id; the same table with its JSON keys written in another order gives the same id; the result directory is `.agent-fox/gate/<id>/`

setup: a fixed tree hash and table
check.pseudocode: k = sha256(tree + canon(table) + 'reduced'); assert Key(tree, table, Reduced).ID == k[:12]; assert Key(..., Hermetic).ID != k[:12]

criteria.condition: `af gate run` runs, `.agent-fox/gate/<id>/result.json` exists for the current key and `--no-cache` is absent
criteria.action: return the stored result with `cached: true` and execute no check
criteria.contract: a counter script used as a check is incremented once across two runs on an unchanged tree; the second envelope has `cached: true`

setup: a git repo with gate.json whose check is a script that appends a line to an ignored counter file outside the view
check.pseudocode: a = af('gate','run'); b = af('gate','run'); assert lines(counter)==1; assert not a.result.cached and b.result.cached; assert a.result.id==b.result.id

criteria.action: for any tree, make the next `af gate run` execute the checks again after any one-byte change to a file in the file view, and serve a cache hit after any change confined to ignored files
criteria.contract: after a viewed-file mutation the counter increments and `cached` is false; after an ignored-file-only mutation the counter does not change and `cached` is true

setup: a generator of small repos and of mutations; a counter-script check
check.pseudocode: for t in gen_repos(): Run(t); m = gen_mutation(t); apply(m); r = Run(t); assert r.cached == (m.kind=='ignored')

criteria.condition: `--no-cache` is given
criteria.action: run the checks and replace the stored result
criteria.contract: `cached: false`; result.json reflects the new run

setup: a cached result for the tree from a counter-script check
check.pseudocode: af('gate','run'); af('gate','run','--no-cache'); assert lines(counter)==2; assert load(resultJson).cached==false

criteria.action: store only completed results, writing `result.json` after all its logs via a temporary file in the same directory followed by rename, so that concurrent runs without locking leave the last writer's complete file and never a partial one
criteria.contract: every successful read of result.json is complete valid JSON; at the end result.json exists and its logs exist; no temporary files remain in `.agent-fox/gate/<id>/`; a result.json never appears before the first log of its run exists

setup: a repo with a check taking ~200ms
10 concurrent gate runs with --no-cache on the same tree while a reader repeatedly parses result.json
check.pseudocode: parallel(10, Run(noCache)); while running: if exists(rj): json.load(rj); assert no tmp files

criteria.condition: `--label L` is given with a valid label
criteria.action: record L mapped to the result id in `.agent-fox/gate/labels.json`, written via temporary file and rename, on a cache hit as well as a miss, replacing any earlier id for L
criteria.contract: `label` in the result equals L; labels.json maps L to the latest id

setup: a repo with a counter check, no labels.json
check.pseudocode: r1=af(...,'--label','baseline'); touch(f); r2=af(...,'--label','baseline'); r3=af(...,'--label','after'); L=load(labels); assert L.baseline==r2.id and L.after==r3.id and r3.cached

criteria.condition: `--label` does not match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$` or is exactly 12 lowercase hex characters
criteria.action: reject the invocation before running any check
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit 2; labels.json unchanged

setup: a repo with an existing labels.json and a counter check
check.pseudocode: for l in bad: env,code=af('gate','run','--label',l); assert code==2 and env.status=='usage'; assert counter_unchanged and labels_bytes_unchanged

requirements.title: af gate compare
requirements.rationale: Landing and Closes-versus-Refs are decided from a measured verdict, computed per check so one fixed and one broken check reads as a regression.

criteria.condition: `af gate compare --before B --after A [--dir D]` runs
criteria.action: resolve each argument as a label in labels.json first and then as a gate id, load both stored results, and compute a per-check verdict matched by check name: pass→pass `pass`, not pass→pass `pass_was_already_failing`, pass→not pass `regressed`, not pass→not pass `still_failing`, where `fail`, `error` and `timeout` count as not pass
criteria.contract: one row per check name with before status, after status and verdict

setup: stored results with checks a,b,c,d,e,f whose before/after statuses are pass/pass, fail/pass, pass/fail, fail/fail, error/pass, pass/timeout
one result stored under a label and the other by its id
check.pseudocode: rows = Compare(dir,'baseline',after.id).rows; assert [r.verdict for r in rows] == [...]

criteria.action: set the overall `verdict` to the first of `regressed`, `still_failing`, `pass_was_already_failing`, `pass` that any row carries, and `landable` to true only for `pass` and `pass_was_already_failing`
criteria.contract: verdict equals the first of regressed, still_failing, pass_was_already_failing, pass that any row carries; landable is true iff verdict is pass or pass_was_already_failing

setup: a generator of result pairs with the same non-empty check names and random statuses from pass, fail, error, timeout
check.pseudocode: for (b,a) in gen_pairs(): v = Compare(b,a); assert v.verdict == first(p for p in ORDER if p in rowverdicts(v)); assert v.landable == (v.verdict in ('pass','pass_was_already_failing'))

criteria.condition: either result has no checks
criteria.action: set the verdict to `unverified`
criteria.contract: `verdict: unverified`, `landable: false`

setup: stored results: one with checks and one with an empty checks list, in both orders; and both empty
check.pseudocode: assert Compare(empty, full).verdict=='unverified' and not .landable

criteria.action: return a result carrying both results' `id`, `label` and `passed`, the overall `verdict`, `landable` and the per-check rows, with status `done` for every verdict
criteria.contract: exit 0 for each of the five verdicts

setup: a repo where gate runs, labelled, have produced result pairs for pass, pass_was_already_failing, regressed, still_failing, and (with an empty-table gate.json) unverified
check.pseudocode: for pair in pairs: env,code = af('gate','compare','--before',pair.b,'--after',pair.a); assert code==0 and env.status=='done' and env.result.verdict==pair.expected

criteria.condition: `--before` or `--after` is missing, or resolves to neither a known label nor a stored id
criteria.action: refuse to compare
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit 2; error.message names the missing or unresolved argument

setup: a repo with one stored label `baseline`
check.pseudocode: env,code = af('gate','compare','--before','baseline','--after','nosuch'); assert code==2 and 'nosuch' in env.error.message

criteria.condition: the two results' sets of check names differ
criteria.action: refuse to compare
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit 2; error.message lists the check names present on only one side

setup: two stored results from different tables: {lint,test} and {test,build}
check.pseudocode: env,code = af('gate','compare',...); assert code==2 and 'lint' in msg and 'build' in msg

requirements.title: af revert-check
requirements.rationale: A fix closes an issue only when its tests are shown to fail without the rest of the change, and the measurement must never cost the caller their tree.

criteria.condition: `--dir` is not the top level of a git work tree, or `--since` is missing or does not resolve to a commit
criteria.action: refuse before touching any file
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit 2; error.message names the wrong argument

setup: a git repo with a subdirectory and an untouched tree, index and .agent-fox
check.pseudocode: for args in cases: env,code = af(*args); assert code==2 and env.status=='usage'; assert state_unchanged()

criteria.action: classify a path as a test path when it matches Go `_test.go` or `testdata/`, Python `test_*.py`, `*_test.py` or `conftest.py`, JavaScript/TypeScript `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*` or `__tests__/`, Java `src/test/`, `*Test.java`, `*Tests.java` or `*IT.java`, Ruby `*_spec.rb` or `*_test.rb`, or has a `test`, `tests` or `spec` directory segment
criteria.contract: true for `a_test.go`, `pkg/testdata/x.json`, `test_a.py`, `a_test.py`, `conftest.py`, `a.test.ts`, `b.spec.js`, `__tests__/x.js`, `src/test/java/A.java`, `FooTest.java`, `FooTests.java`, `FooIT.java`, `x_spec.rb`, `x_test.rb`, `tests/a.rs`, `spec/x.rb`, `a/test/b.c`; false for `main.go`, `latest.go`, `contest.py`, `src/main/java/A.java`, `testing.md` and `attest/x.go`

setup: a table of positive and negative paths
check.pseudocode: for p in pos: assert IsTestPath(p); for p in neg: assert not IsTestPath(p)

criteria.condition: `af revert-check --since R` lists the changed paths (NUL-separated, untracked included) and nothing can be measured
criteria.action: return without modifying any file the outcome `no_changes` when no path changed, `no_code_changes` when only test paths changed, `no_test_changes` when no test path changed, or `inconclusive` when the table has no check of kind `test` or `check`
criteria.contract: status `done`, exit 0; `restored: true`; warning `fix_not_proven` for every outcome except `no_changes`

setup: a git repo with a base commit and gate.json with a test check
case A: no changes; B: only test files changed; C: only non-test files changed; D: test and non-test changed but gate.json has only a lint check
check.pseudocode: for c in cases: env = af('revert-check','--since',base); assert env.result.outcome==c.outcome; assert ('fix_not_proven' in codes) == (c.outcome!='no_changes'); assert unchanged()

criteria.condition: changed test and non-test paths exist and the table has a `test` or `check` check
criteria.action: take the full table's result for the current tree from the gate cache or run and cache it, and when any of its `test` or `check` checks did not pass return outcome `inconclusive` with reason `after_not_green` without reverting
criteria.contract: status `done`; `after` holds the gate id; warning `fix_not_proven`

setup: a git repo whose change touches a source file and a test file, and whose test check fails on the current tree
check.pseudocode: env = af('revert-check','--since',base); assert env.result.reason=='after_not_green'; assert exists('.agent-fox/gate/'+env.result.after+'/result.json'); assert env.result.reverted_files==[]

criteria.condition: the current tree's `test` and `check` checks passed
criteria.action: copy every existing non-test changed path into `.agent-fox/revert/<id>/` with a manifest, then without touching the index give each non-test path present at R the ref's content and mode (read via `git show` and `git ls-tree -z`), move aside each non-test path absent at R, leave test paths as they are, and run only the `test` and `check` checks through the gate engine cached by the reverted tree's hash
criteria.contract: `reverted_files` lists the reverted paths; `test_files` lists the test paths

setup: a base commit with `lib.sh` (mode 755, content v1) and a test script `check_test.sh`
a working tree where lib.sh is v2, a new non-test file `new.go` is untracked, a test `fix_test.go` is added, and the current tree is green
a gate.json test check that, when run, records whether lib.sh holds v1, whether new.go exists and whether fix_test.go exists, into an ignored file
check.pseudocode: env = af('revert-check','--since',base); obs = read(observation); assert obs.libContent=='v1' and obs.libMode==0o755 and not obs.newExists and obs.testExists; assert env.result.reverted_files==['lib.sh','new.go']

criteria.action: set outcome `proven` when any reverted-tree check fails and `not_proven` when all pass, set `closes` true only for `proven`, emit warning `fix_not_proven` for every outcome other than `proven` and `no_changes`, and return `outcome`, `reason`, `closes`, `since` (resolved to a full hash), `test_files`, `reverted_files`, `after`, the reverted gate result (`id`, `passed`, `checks`) and `restored`
criteria.contract: status `done`, exit 0 for both `proven` and `not_proven`

setup: fixture P: change adds a fix to lib file and a test that fails without it
fixture N: change adds a test that passes without the fix
check.pseudocode: p = af(P); assert p.result.outcome=='proven' and p.result.closes and len(p.result.since)==40; n = af(N); assert n.result.outcome=='not_proven' and not n.result.closes

criteria.action: after reverting, restore every reverted and moved-aside path from the backup using a context that is not cancelled, verify that the tree hash equals the hash taken before the revert and that the index is byte-identical to its pre-revert state, then remove the backup directory, in every outcome including cancellation by signal or `--timeout` mid-run
criteria.contract: after the command returns the tree hash and the `.git/index` bytes equal their values before the command; `restored: true`

setup: a generator of repos with random mixes of modified, added, deleted-and-renamed source files and test files, staged and unstaged, with a test check that passes or fails by content
a proven-style fixture whose reverted-tree test check sleeps 60s
the command run with `--timeout 3s` (and a variant killed by SIGINT once the reverted check starts)
check.pseudocode:
for repo in gen_repos(): h=TreeHash(repo); ix=read(repo/.git/index); Check(repo, base); assert TreeHash(repo)==h and read(index)==ix and not exists(repo/.agent-fox/revert/*)
env,code = af('revert-check','--since',base,'--timeout','3s'); assert TreeHash(dir)==h0 and read(index)==ix0 and not exists(backup)

criteria.condition: the restore fails, the restored tree hash differs from the pre-revert hash, or a directory under `.agent-fox/revert/` already exists when the command starts
criteria.action: stop, keep every backup directory in place and revert nothing further
criteria.contract: status `failed`, exit 1, error.category `restore`; error.message names the backup directory

setup: case A: a directory `.agent-fox/revert/old/` exists before the command starts
case B: the test check deletes the backup directory's copy of a file (or makes the target path unwritable) so that the restore fails or the hash differs
check.pseudocode: env,code = af('revert-check','--since',base); assert code==1 and env.error.category=='restore' and backupDir in env.error.message and exists(backupDir)

requirements.title: Guard decisions on shell commands
requirements.rationale: A brain must not run the suite the gate caches, mutate git or call loop commands, and the rules this scope tests must not depend on the unread hands' guard semantics.

criteria.condition: a shell tool call (Claude Code `Bash` or the hands' `execute`) is decided
criteria.action: tokenize the command with a standard-library POSIX-quoting tokenizer, split it into segments on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, `&` and newlines, inspect the contents of `$(…)`, backticks and `sh|bash|zsh -c '…'` as further segments, skip leading `VAR=value` assignments and the wrappers `env`, `time`, `timeout`, `nice`, `nohup`, `command` and `exec` to find each segment's program, and evaluate rules 1–7 in order per segment with the first deny winning
criteria.contract: a decision `allow` or `deny` with `rule`, `segment` and `reason`

setup: a policy whose suite contains `go test ./...` and default protected paths
check.pseudocode: for c in denied: d = Decide(bash(c)); assert d.Decision=='deny' and d.Segment!=''; assert Decide(bash('go test ./pkg -run X; git diff')).Decision=='allow'

criteria.condition: the command cannot be parsed, for example it has unbalanced quotes or an unterminated `$(`
criteria.action: deny the call
criteria.contract: decision `deny`, rule `unparseable`

setup: default policy
check.pseudocode: for c in bad: d=Decide(bash(c)); assert d.Decision=='deny' and d.Rule=='unparseable'

criteria.condition: the hands' `guard.Check`, called through one adapter as a deny-only first layer, refuses the command
criteria.action: deny the call and pass the hands' reason through; an allow from the hands never overrides a later rule
criteria.contract: decision `deny`, rule `hands_guard`, reason equal to the hands' reason

setup: the hands' guard adapter replaced by a stub that refuses `rm -rf /` with reason R and allows everything else
check.pseudocode: setHands(stub); d=Decide(bash('rm -rf /')); assert d.Rule=='hands_guard' and d.Reason==R; assert Decide(bash('git push')).Rule=='git_mutation'

criteria.condition: a segment's program is `git`
criteria.action: allow only the subcommands `status`, `log`, `diff`, `show`, `blame`, `ls-files`, `ls-tree`, `rev-parse`, `rev-list`, `grep`, `describe`, `cat-file`, `shortlog`, `merge-base`, `name-rev`, `for-each-ref` and `show-ref`, plus `branch` and `remote` in their listing forms only, and deny any other subcommand or a global `-c` with a reason saying that `af` makes every commit, branch and push
criteria.contract: `git diff` allowed; `git commit` and `git push` denied with rule `git_mutation`

setup: default policy
check.pseudocode: for s in RO: assert Decide(bash('git '+s)).Decision=='allow'; d=Decide(bash('git commit -m x')); assert d.Rule=='git_mutation' and 'af' in d.Reason

criteria.condition: a segment equals a suite form once every token starting with `-` is removed from both
criteria.action: deny the segment with a reason that names the command, says to run `af gate run` instead because it caches the result by tree hash and the landing reuses it, and says that targeted runs are allowed
criteria.contract: rule `suite_command`; `make check`, `go test ./...` and `go test -count=1 ./...` denied; `go test ./internal/x -run TestY` allowed

setup: a policy whose suite holds `make check`, `make test`, `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`
check.pseudocode: d=Decide(bash('go test -count=1 ./...')); assert d.Rule=='suite_command' and 'af gate run' in d.Reason and 'targeted' in d.Reason; assert Decide(bash('go test ./internal/x -run TestY')).Decision=='allow'

criteria.condition: a segment's program is `af`
criteria.action: allow only `lang detect`, `gate run`, `gate compare`, `revert-check`, `map`, `guard check`, `triage brief`, `triage submit`, `fix brief`, `fix submit`, `--version` and `--schema`, and deny any other `af` command as belonging to the loop
criteria.contract: `af gate run` allowed; `af fix land` denied with rule `af_command`

setup: default policy
check.pseudocode: for c in ALLOWED: assert Decide(bash(c)).Decision=='allow'; d=Decide(bash('af fix land')); assert d.Rule=='af_command'

criteria.condition: the policy's `allow_programs` is not empty
criteria.action: deny a segment whose program is outside `allow_programs`, with `af` and `git` always permitted
criteria.contract: decision `deny`, rule `program_not_allowed`

setup: policy A with allow_programs [`go`, `ls`]; policy B with allow_programs empty
check.pseudocode: assert Decide(A, bash('curl x')).Rule=='program_not_allowed'; assert Decide(B, bash('curl x')).Decision=='allow'

criteria.condition: a segment writes into a protected path through an output redirection target or through an argument written by `rm`, `mv`, `cp`, `tee`, `touch`, `mkdir`, `truncate`, `ln`, `chmod` or `sed -i`, resolved against `--dir`
criteria.action: deny the segment
criteria.contract: decision `deny`, rule `protected_path`

setup: dir D with default protected paths
check.pseudocode: for c in bad: assert Decide(bash(c)).Rule=='protected_path'; for c in ok: assert Decide(bash(c)).Decision=='allow'

requirements.title: Guard policy source, write tools and af guard check I/O
requirements.rationale: The same decision must reach the envelope caller, the Claude Code hook and the in-process interceptor, and the hook must fail closed.

criteria.action: load the policy from the first that exists of `--policy <path>`, `<dir>/.agent-fox/guard.json` (`{"version": 1, "suite": [[...]], "protected_paths": [...], "allow_programs": [...]}`), and defaults derived from R2 on `--dir`, filling each missing key with its default: `suite` from R2's suite, `protected_paths` `.git/`, `.agent-fox/`, `.specs/`, `.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, and `allow_programs` empty
criteria.contract: with --policy, P's suite is used even though guard.json exists; with guard.json only, protected_paths is [`docs/`] while suite is the detected suite and allow_programs is empty; with neither, protected_paths are `.git/`, `.agent-fox/`, `.specs/`, `.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, suite is R2's suite and allow_programs is empty

setup: a repo with a Makefile `check` target
a policy file P with suite [[`foo`]]
`.agent-fox/guard.json` with only {"version":1,"protected_paths":["docs/"]}
check.pseudocode: p=Load(dir,policyPath=P); assert p.Suite==[['foo']]; p=Load(dir,''); assert p.ProtectedPaths==['docs/'] and p.Suite==Detect(dir).Suite

criteria.condition: a write tool call (`Write`, `Edit`, `MultiEdit`, `NotebookEdit`, the hands' `write_file` or `edit_file`) is decided
criteria.action: resolve its path against `--dir` and deny it when the path is under a protected path, or when it is outside `--dir` and not under the system temporary directory
criteria.contract: a `Write` to `.specs/x.md` is denied with rule `protected_path`; a write to `/etc/x` is denied with rule `outside_dir`

setup: dir D, default policy, a path under os.TempDir()
check.pseudocode: d=Decide(write('Write','.specs/x.md')); assert d.Rule=='protected_path'; assert Decide(write('Write','/etc/x')).Rule=='outside_dir'

criteria.action: allow every tool call that is neither a shell nor a write tool, and expose the decision function as a plain Go API returning `decision` (`allow`|`deny`), `rule` (one of `unparseable`, `hands_guard`, `git_mutation`, `suite_command`, `af_command`, `program_not_allowed`, `protected_path`, `outside_dir`, empty on allow), the deciding `segment` and a `reason`
criteria.contract: an unknown tool name such as `Read` yields decision `allow` with an empty rule; every deny carries a non-empty rule, segment and reason

setup: default policy
check.pseudocode: assert Decide(tool('Read',{})) == Decision('allow','','','')... ; for d in denies: assert d.Rule in RULES and d.Segment and d.Reason

criteria.condition: `af guard check` reads its stdin
criteria.action: read at most 1 MiB of raw stdin and accept either a Claude Code hook payload (`hook_event_name`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `cwd`) or the neutral form `{"tool": "...", "input": {...}}`, allowing with no opinion a payload whose `hook_event_name` is present and is not `PreToolUse`
criteria.contract: the same payload yields the same decision in envelope and `--host claude` form

setup: the af guard check command in a repo with defaults
check.pseudocode: for form in (claude, neutral): assert decision(form)=='deny'; assert decision(postToolUse)=='allow'

criteria.condition: `--host` is not given
criteria.action: print the envelope with `result` holding `decision`, `rule`, `reason`, `tool` and `segment`
criteria.contract: status `done`, exit 0 for both allow and deny

setup: the af guard check command
check.pseudocode: env,code = af_stdin(deny_payload); assert code==0 and env.status=='done' and env.result.decision=='deny' and env.result.rule=='git_mutation'

criteria.condition: `--host` is not given and the payload is malformed, exceeds 1 MiB, or the policy file does not parse
criteria.action: decide nothing
criteria.contract: malformed or oversized payload: status `usage`, exit 2; unparseable policy: status `failed`, exit 1, error.category `config`

setup: the af guard check command
check.pseudocode: assert code(af_stdin('{not json'))==2; assert code(af_stdin(big))==2; env,c=af_stdin(ok,'--policy',bad); assert c==1 and env.error.category=='config'

criteria.condition: `--host claude` is given
criteria.action: print instead of the envelope `{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "deny", "permissionDecisionReason": "<reason>"}}` for a deny and `{}` for an allow, never emitting `permissionDecision: allow`
criteria.contract: exit 0; stdout is a single JSON document

setup: the af guard check command run as a subprocess
check.pseudocode: out,code = run(['guard','check','--host','claude'], stdin); assert code==0; j=json.loads(out); assert j['hookSpecificOutput']['permissionDecision']=='deny'; assert json.loads(out_allow)=={}

criteria.condition: `--host claude` is given and an internal error occurs (malformed or oversized payload, unparseable policy, or a panic)
criteria.action: answer with a deny whose reason carries the error
criteria.contract: exit 0; stdout `permissionDecision` is `deny`

setup: the af guard check command with --host claude
check.pseudocode: for case in errors: out,code = run(case); assert code==0 and json.loads(out)['hookSpecificOutput']['permissionDecision']=='deny'

requirements.title: af map
requirements.rationale: A brief's run-constant prefix needs a deterministic repository map that never exceeds its token budget.

criteria.condition: `af map [--dir D] [--tokens N]` runs
criteria.action: render the file view in path order with each directory as a `path/` header (root `./`), each file indented two spaces, and each file's declarations after it as `<kind> <name> L<line>` joined by ` · `, estimating tokens as the byte count divided by 4 rounded up, with N defaulting to 4000
criteria.contract: status `done`, exit 0

setup: a file view `a.go`, `pkg/b.go`, `pkg/b_test.go` and a fake Outliner returning `func A L3`, `type T L10` for a.go and `func B L1` for pkg/b.go
budget 4000
a repo with a few files
check.pseudocode:
r = Build(view, fake, 4000); assert r.Level==1 and r.EstimatedTokens==ceil(len(r.Map)/4) and not r.Truncated and 'func A L3 · type T L10' in r.Map
assert af('map').result.tokens==4000; assert code(af('map','--tokens','199'))==2

criteria.condition: `--tokens` is below 200 or above 100000
criteria.action: refuse to render
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit 2

criteria.action: take declarations from an `Outliner` interface implemented by one adapter over the hands' outline, and list by name only any file the outliner rejects (unsupported language, parse error, or larger than 1 MiB)
criteria.contract: a rejected file appears in `map` by name only and is not counted in `files_outlined`; the command still returns status `done`

setup: a fake Outliner that returns an unsupported-language error for `x.txt`, a parse error for `bad.go`, and declarations for `ok.go`
a file `big.go` over 1 MiB
check.pseudocode: r,err = Build(...); assert err==nil and r.FilesOutlined==1 and 'bad.go\n' in r.Map; assert 'big.go' not in fake.calls

criteria.action: emit the first ladder level whose output fits the budget: 1 every file with every declaration; 2 test files without declarations; 3 other files' declarations capped at K (20, 10, 5, 2, 1) with `… +N more`; 4 every file by name only; 5 directories only as `path/ (N files)`; 6 directories cut off at the budget followed by `… N more directories`
criteria.contract: `level` equals the emitted ladder level

setup: a fake file view with many files, tests and declarations, and per-level fixture budgets measured from each level's rendered size
check.pseudocode: for lvl,budget in fixtures: assert Build(view,fake,budget).Level==lvl

criteria.action: for any file view, outliner output and budget N in [200, 100000], produce output whose estimated tokens are at most N, and produce byte-identical output for the same tree and budget
criteria.contract: estimated_tokens <= N and ceil(len(map)/4) <= N; the two outputs are byte-identical; the reported level equals the first fitting level

setup: a generator of file views (up to a few thousand paths with long names), fake outliner outputs and budgets in [200, 100000]
check.pseudocode: for (v,o,n) in gen(): a=Build(v,o,n); b=Build(v,o,n); assert ceil(len(a.Map)/4)<=n and a.Map==b.Map

criteria.condition: the name-only rendering already exceeds the budget or the file view holds more than 5000 files
criteria.action: skip calling the outliner
criteria.contract: coded warning `map_outline_skipped`; `files_outlined: 0`

setup: a counting fake Outliner
case A: 3000 long-named files with budget 200; case B: 5001 short files with budget 100000
check.pseudocode: r = Build(...); assert fake.calls==0 and r.FilesOutlined==0 and 'map_outline_skipped' in r.WarningCodes

criteria.action: return a result holding `map`, `tokens` (the budget), `estimated_tokens`, `level`, `files_total`, `files_outlined` and `truncated` (true for any level above 1)

requirements.title: Shell wiring, offline operation, schemas and docs
requirements.rationale: The six commands inherit the spec-05 contract, stay usable in-process by later loops, and ship documented and tested offline.

criteria.action: register `lang detect`, `gate run`, `gate compare`, `revert-check`, `guard check` and `map` on the spec-05 `toolio` shell in `cmd/af`, using its envelope, exit codes, coded warnings, `--dir` and `--timeout`, with default timeouts of 1 minute, 30 minutes, 30 seconds, 30 minutes, 10 seconds and 2 minutes respectively
criteria.contract: each command's `--help` lists its flags; each envelope's `tool` equals its command path

setup: the built af shell
check.pseudocode: for cmd in six: assert cmd.DefaultTimeout==expected[cmd]; out=af(cmd,'--help'); for f in flags[cmd]: assert f in out; assert af(cmd,...).tool==cmd

criteria.action: build no forge client, call no model and open no network connection in any of the six commands, and create no run directory
criteria.contract: no `.agent-fox/run/` directory is created by any of the six commands

setup: a repo with no remote, env with forge tokens unset, HTTP(S) proxy variables pointing to a closed local port, and a listener recording any connection attempt
check.pseudocode: for c in six: af(c); assert listener.conns==0; assert not exists('.agent-fox/run')

criteria.action: keep `internal/project`, `internal/checks`, `internal/conform`, `internal/policy` and `internal/repomap` free of any import of `internal/toolio`, returning plain Go results and errors and never calling `os.Exit` or panicking on bad input
criteria.contract: no file imports `internal/toolio`; no non-test file calls `os.Exit` or `log.Fatal`

setup: the Go source of internal/project, checks, conform, policy and repomap
check.pseudocode: for f in files: ast=parse(f); assert 'internal/toolio' not in imports(ast); assert not calls(ast,'os.Exit')

criteria.action: embed a result JSON schema for each of the six commands, include it in `af --schema`, regenerate the committed `--schema` golden once while keeping the envelope schema version unchanged, and fail a test when a schema's top-level properties and the JSON fields of the command's Go result type differ
criteria.contract: `af --schema` output equals the committed golden

setup: the six embedded result schemas and Go result types
the committed `--schema` golden
check.pseudocode: for c in six: assert keys(schema[c].properties) == jsonFields(reflect.TypeOf(c.Result)); assert af('--schema') == read(golden)

criteria.condition: the spec-05 `toolio` shell lacks raw stdin access for a command without positional input, or a way for a command to supply its own stdout document
criteria.action: add the smallest extension providing each missing capability, used only by `af guard check --host claude`
criteria.contract: every other command's output remains an envelope

setup: the shell with the raw stdin and command-supplied stdout capabilities
check.pseudocode: for c in others: assert 'status' in json(af(c)); assert 'status' not in json(af('guard','check','--host','claude'))

criteria.condition: a command fails for a reason other than usage
criteria.action: report it with one of the failure categories `config`, `restore`, `git` or `io`, extending the spec-05 category set when it is closed
criteria.contract: status `failed`, exit 1, error.category in {config, restore, git, io}

setup: failure cases: broken gate.json (config), leftover revert backup (restore), --dir that is not a repository for revert-check with a valid --since format but git failing (git), a .agent-fox path that cannot be written (io)
check.pseudocode: for case in cases: env,code=af(*case.args); assert code==1 and env.error.category==case.category

criteria.action: test every criterion of this spec offline within `make check`, using temporary git repositories built like `gitx`'s `newRepo` and skipped when git is missing, gate checks that are small scripts or `go` invocations with a counter file, a fake `Outliner`, and payload fixtures for both payload forms
criteria.contract: `make check` passes with no network and no credentials

setup: the test files of the five internal packages, gitx and cmd/af for this spec
check.pseudocode: for f in test_files: assert not imports_nonlocal_net(f); with PATH='': run tests -> exit 0 (skipped)

criteria.action: after running `make doc`, describe the commands, flags, results, rules and warning codes in `docs/cli.md`, the `gate.json` and `guard.json` formats and precedence in `docs/configuration.md`, that these commands call no model in `docs/model-usage.md`, the new packages and the `.agent-fox/gate/` and `.agent-fox/revert/` layout in `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/development.md` (created if absent), and the package table in `README.md`
criteria.contract: no TODO or TBD text in those files

setup: docs/cli.md, docs/configuration.md, docs/model-usage.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/development.md and README.md after `make doc`
check.pseudocode: for f,terms in EXPECT: t=read(f); for x in terms: assert x in t; assert 'TODO' not in t and 'TBD' not in t

execution_paths.title: A person detects languages and the gate table of a repository

steps.action: runs `af lang detect --dir repo --write`
parses flags, applies the 1-minute timeout and dispatches to the lang detect command
builds the file view, counts languages and detects the gate table from the root Makefile or manifests
writes `.agent-fox/gate.json` atomically
prints a `done` envelope with languages, gate, suite and programs and exits 0

setup: the built af binary
a git repo with a Makefile `check` target and Go sources
end_state: a `done` envelope (tool `lang detect`) with languages, gate (source detected, [make check]), suite and programs, exit 0
`.agent-fox/gate.json` exists with version 1 and the table, and `git status` shows nothing from `.agent-fox/`
a second `af lang detect` reports source `file`

execution_paths.title: The loop runs the gate twice under labels, hits the cache, and compares

steps.action: runs `af gate run --label baseline` on a tree with a red counter-script check
computes the tree hash and cache key, runs the check under ReducedEnvRunner, writes its log and stores result.json and labels.json atomically
fixes the file and runs `af gate run --label after`, then repeats it on the unchanged tree
returns the stored result with `cached: true` without executing the counter script again
runs `af gate compare --before baseline --after after`
resolves both labels and prints a `done` envelope with verdict `pass_was_already_failing` and `landable: true`

setup: the built af binary
a git repo with gate.json holding a counter-script check that fails until a marker file exists in the tree
end_state: baseline result is `done` with passed false
the second `after` run is `cached: true` and the counter shows no extra execution
labels.json maps baseline and after to different ids
compare prints a `done` envelope with verdict `pass_was_already_failing`, landable true, exit 0

execution_paths.title: The loop proves a fix with the revert check and gets the tree back

steps.action: runs `af revert-check --since <base>` in a repository whose change adds a fix and a test that fails without it
lists changed paths NUL-separated, classifies test paths and measures the current tree green through the gate cache
backs up and reverts the non-test paths without touching the index, then runs the test checks on the reverted tree
restores from the backup, verifies the tree hash and index are unchanged, and removes `.agent-fox/revert/<id>/`
prints a `done` envelope with outcome `proven`, `closes: true` and `restored: true`

setup: the built af binary
a git repo whose HEAD~ is the base, with a working-tree change adding a fix in a source file and a test that fails without it, partly staged
gate.json with a `go test`-style or script test check
end_state: a `done` envelope with outcome `proven`, closes true, restored true, exit 0
the tree hash and `.git/index` bytes equal their values before the command
the same repo with a passing-without-fix test gives `not_proven` with warning `fix_not_proven`

execution_paths.title: Claude Code's PreToolUse hook asks the guard about a suite command

steps.action: pipes a PreToolUse payload with tool `Bash` and command `go test ./...` to `af guard check --host claude`
reads the raw stdin payload and loads the policy from guard.json or detection defaults
tokenizes the command, applies the hands' guard adapter and the af rules, and denies with rule `suite_command`
prints the hookSpecificOutput deny document naming `af gate run` and exits 0

setup: the built af binary
a repo with a Makefile `check` target and go.mod

steps.action: runs `af map --tokens 400`
builds the file view and asks the Outliner for each file's declarations
walks the reduction ladder and selects the first level within 400 estimated tokens
prints a `done` envelope with the map text, its level and estimated tokens
